perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- He knows Gary Guo as a close, long-time friend from middle school.
- He has observed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep.
- Concerned, Ethan invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- He heard Gary decline, saying he appreciated Ethan’s concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- During the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work.
- Ethan suspected Gary’s overworking was about more than professional obligations. He confronted Gary, telling him they had been friends since middle school and he could tell him anything without judgment.
- He heard Gary say it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan with his problems.
- Gary then opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- Ethan felt relief and empathy, and offered to help Gary find a better balance.
- Ethan advised Gary to prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, and offered continued support.
- He heard Gary say things were better, that he was less overwhelmed thanks to Ethan’s help, and that he had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- Ethan felt hopeful and proud of Gary’s progress.
- After a year, Ethan saw that Gary was managing a healthier work-life balance on his own. He felt satisfied and happy for Gary, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always a call away if needed.
- He heard Gary thank him, say he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and that he felt more in control now.
